grammar.q: My brother ___ coffee. He only drinks tea.
grammar.why: He/she/it bilan Present Simple inkorida "doesn't" + feʼlning asosiy shakli (-s qoʻshimchasiz) ishlatiladi.

grammar.q: Sorry, I can't talk right now. I ___ dinner.
grammar.why: "Right now" ayni paytda davom etayotgan ishni bildiradi, shuning uchun Present Continuous (am/is/are + -ing) kerak.

grammar.q: We ___ to Samarkand last weekend.
grammar.why: "Last weekend" tugagan oʻtgan vaqtni koʻrsatadi, shuning uchun Past Simple kerak; "go" notoʻgʻri feʼl, uning oʻtgan zamon shakli "went".

grammar.q: What time ___ you get home last night?
grammar.why: Past Simple soʻroq gapi "did" + feʼlning asosiy shakli bilan tuziladi; "was/were" faqat "be" feʼlining oʻzi kesim boʻlganda ishlatiladi.

grammar.q: This apartment is ___ than our old one.
grammar.why: Qisqa (bir boʻgʻinli) sifatlarning qiyosiy darajasi -er qoʻshimchasi bilan yasaladi: big - bigger; "more" faqat uzun sifatlar bilan keladi.

grammar.q: ___ two banks on this street.
grammar.why: Biror joyda nimadir borligini aytish uchun "there is/are" ishlatiladi; koʻplikdagi ot (two banks) bilan "there are" keladi.

grammar.q: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early tonight.
grammar.why: Maslahat "should" bilan beriladi va undan keyin feʼl "to" yuklamasisiz keladi; "need" va "have" esa "to" ni talab qiladi.

grammar.q: I already bought the tickets. I ___ visit my parents this weekend.
grammar.why: Oldindan rejalashtirilgan ish "be going to" + feʼl bilan aytiladi; "be" feʼlini (am/is/are) tushirib qoldirib boʻlmaydi.

grammar.q: How ___ money do you have with you?
grammar.why: "Money" sanalmaydigan ot, shuning uchun "how much" ishlatiladi; "how many" faqat sanaladigan koʻplikdagi otlar bilan keladi.

grammar.q: There isn't ___ milk in the fridge.
grammar.why: Inkor gaplarda "some" emas, "any" ishlatiladi; "isn't" bilan "no" qoʻshilsa, inkor ikki marta takrorlanib qoladi.

grammar.q: My flight is ___ Friday.
grammar.why: Hafta kunlari va sanalar oldidan "on" predlogi keladi: on Friday, on Monday.

grammar.q: She's waiting for us ___ the bus stop.
grammar.why: Aniq bir nuqta yoki manzil (bekat, eshik oldi, chorraha) haqida gapirganda "at" ishlatiladi: at the bus stop.

grammar.q: Madina ___ at this company since 2019.
grammar.why: Oʻtmishda boshlanib, hozir ham davom etayotgan ish "since" bilan Present Perfect da aytiladi; oʻzbek va rus tillaridagidek hozirgi zamon ishlatilmaydi.

grammar.q: I ___ the invoice to the client two days ago.
grammar.why: "Two days ago" kabi aniq tugagan vaqt bilan Present Perfect emas, Past Simple ishlatiladi; "send" notoʻgʻri feʼl: send - sent.

grammar.q: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll cancel the picnic.
grammar.why: Birinchi shart gapda "if" dan keyin kelasi zamon maʼnosida ham Present Simple keladi; "will" faqat bosh gapda ishlatiladi.

grammar.q: If I ___ more free time, I would learn to play the guitar.
grammar.why: Ikkinchi shart gap (hozirgi noreal vaziyat): "if" + Past Simple, bosh gapda "would" + feʼl; "if" dan keyin "would" qoʻyilmaydi.

grammar.q: These phones ___ in Vietnam.
grammar.why: Telefonlar oʻzi ishlab chiqarmaydi, ularni ishlab chiqarishadi, shuning uchun majhul nisbat kerak: am/is/are + feʼlning 3-shakli (are made).

grammar.q: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
grammar.why: Odam haqidagi aniqlovchi ergash gap "who" bilan bogʻlanadi; "which" faqat narsalar uchun, "what" esa bunday bogʻlovchi boʻla olmaydi.

grammar.q: I ___ play soccer every weekend when I was a kid, but now I don't have time.
grammar.why: Oʻtmishda odat boʻlgan, hozir esa qilinmaydigan ish "used to" + feʼl bilan aytiladi; "be used to" esa "koʻnikkan boʻlmoq" degan boshqa maʼnoni beradi.

grammar.q: Tomorrow is a holiday, so we ___ go to work.
grammar.why: "don't have to" - shart emas, majburiyat yoʻq degani; "mustn't" esa taqiqni (mumkin emas) bildiradi.

grammar.q: I'm not sure where Dave is. He ___ be in a meeting.
grammar.why: Aniq bilmagan taxminimizni "might" + feʼl bilan aytamiz; "maybe" ravish boʻlib, gap boshida keladi va modal feʼl oʻrnini bosa olmaydi.

grammar.q: I really enjoy ___ with numbers.
grammar.why: "Enjoy" feʼlidan keyin ikkinchi feʼl har doim -ing shaklida keladi: enjoy working.

grammar.q: The receptionist asked me what time ___.
grammar.why: Oʻzlashtirma soʻroq gapda soʻz tartibi darak gapdagidek boʻladi (ega + kesim), yordamchi "did" ishlatilmaydi va zamon bir pogʻona orqaga suriladi.

grammar.q: Sorry I didn't answer. I ___ when you called.
grammar.why: Oʻtmishda bir ish yuz bergan paytda davom etib turgan boshqa ish Past Continuous (was/were + -ing) bilan ifodalanadi.

grammar.q: If we ___ earlier, we wouldn't have missed the flight.
grammar.why: Uchinchi shart gap (oʻtmishdagi noreal vaziyat): "if" + Past Perfect (had left), bosh gapda "would have" + 3-shakl; "if" dan keyin "would" kelmaydi.

grammar.q: If I had taken that job in Dubai, I ___ there now.
grammar.why: Aralash shart gap: shart oʻtmishga (had taken), natija esa hozirga (now) tegishli, shuning uchun bosh gapda "would have" emas, "would" + feʼl ishlatiladi.

grammar.q: I wish I ___ speak Spanish. It would really help me at work.
grammar.why: "Wish" dan keyin hozirgi noreal istak uchun feʼl bir zamon orqaga suriladi: can - could.

grammar.q: By the time we got to the theater, the movie ___.
grammar.why: Oʻtmishdagi bir ishdan (got) oldinroq boʻlib oʻtgan ish Past Perfect (had + 3-shakl) bilan aytiladi.

grammar.q: When I finally got to the restaurant, my friends ___ for forty minutes.
grammar.why: Oʻtmishdagi bir paytgacha maʼlum muddat davom etgan ish Past Perfect Continuous (had been + -ing) bilan ifodalanadi.

grammar.q: All invoices ___ by the end of the month.
grammar.why: Modal feʼl bilan majhul nisbat: modal + be + 3-shakl (must be paid); hisob-fakturalar oʻzi toʻlamaydi, ularni toʻlashadi.

grammar.q: The meeting ___ until Thursday, so we have two more days to prepare.
grammar.why: Present Perfect majhul nisbati: have/has + been + 3-shakl; yigʻilish oʻzi koʻchmaydi, uni kimdir keyinga qoldirgan.

grammar.q: I don't fix my car myself. I ___ at a shop near my office.
grammar.why: Ishni boshqa odamga qildirganimizda "have" + narsa + 3-shakl qurilmasi ishlatiladi: have it fixed.

grammar.q: ___ the heavy traffic, we got to the airport on time.
grammar.why: "Despite" dan keyin ot yoki ot birikmasi keladi (the heavy traffic); "although" va "even though" esa ega va kesimli gapni talab qiladi.

grammar.q: I'm so tired this morning. I ___ to bed earlier last night.
grammar.why: Oʻtmishda qilinmay qolgan ish uchun afsus "should have" + 3-shakl bilan aytiladi.

grammar.q: The streets are all wet this morning. It ___ last night.
grammar.why: Dalilga asoslangan oʻtmish haqidagi ishonchli taxmin "must have" + 3-shakl bilan ifodalanadi; "had to" esa majburiyatni bildiradi.

grammar.q: The manager suggested ___ the meeting to Friday.
grammar.why: "Suggest" feʼlidan keyin infinitiv emas, -ing shakli (yoki "that" + toʻliq gap) keladi: suggested moving.

listening.intro: Juma kuni ishda ikki hamkasb - Sarah va Aziz dam olish kunlariga rejalari haqida gaplashyapti.

lines.t: Hey Aziz, do you have any plans for the weekend?
Yeah, I'm going to visit my parents on Saturday. They live about two hours from here.
Nice! Are you driving?
No, my car is at the shop, so I'm taking the train. It leaves at 8:30 in the morning.
That's early! What about Sunday?
On Sunday I'm staying home. I need to clean my apartment and buy some food for next week. What about you?
My sister is in town, so we're going to that new Italian place downtown on Saturday night.
Oh, I went there last month. The pasta is great, but it's a little expensive.
Good to know. Do I need a reservation?
Yes, definitely. It's always full on weekends.
OK, I'll call them right now. Thanks!

q.q: Where is Aziz going on Saturday?
q.why: Aziz "I'm going to visit my parents on Saturday" deydi; italyan restoraniga esa Sarah singlisi bilan boradi.
Mashinasi ustaxonada, shuning uchun u poyezdda ketyapti: "I'm taking the train".

o: Clean his apartment and buy food
Pick up his car from the shop
q.q: What is Aziz going to do on Sunday?
q.why: Yakshanba kuni u uyda qoladi: kvartirasini tozalashi va kelasi hafta uchun oziq-ovqat olishi kerak.

o: It's cheap, and it's never busy
It's new, and he hasn't been there yet
The food is good, but it costs a lot
q.q: What does Aziz say about the Italian restaurant?
q.why: U "The pasta is great, but it's a little expensive" deydi, yaʼni taomi yaxshi, lekin narxi qimmatroq.

listening.title: Weekend Plans

listening.intro: Rachel mijoz bilan telefonda gaplashib boʻlgach, hamkasbi Jasurning oldiga keladi.

lines.t: Jasur, do you have a minute? I just got off the phone with the client.
Sure. That doesn't sound good. What's up?
Well, they want to move the presentation up. Instead of next Wednesday, they're asking for this Friday.
This Friday? Rachel, we haven't even finished the cost section yet. I was planning to work on it over the weekend.
I know, I know. I told them it was short notice, but their director is flying out on Saturday, and she wants to see the numbers before she leaves.
Hmm. If I drop everything else, I could probably have the costs ready by Thursday afternoon. But somebody would have to cover my monthly report.
I already asked Emily, and she said she'd take care of it.
OK, that helps. One more thing, though. I promised my daughter I'd be at her school concert on Thursday at six. I really can't miss that.
You won't have to. Just send me whatever you have by five, and I'll put the slides together myself that evening.
All right, deal. But next time, maybe don't pick up the phone when they call.
Ha! I'll think about it.

o: They are unhappy with the cost section
Their director is leaving town on Saturday
They need more time to prepare
Rachel offered them an earlier date
q.q: Why does the client want the presentation on Friday?
q.why: Mijozning direktori shanba kuni uchib ketadi va ketishidan oldin raqamlarni koʻrmoqchi.

o: Someone to take over his monthly report
q.q: What does Jasur need in order to finish the costs by Thursday?
q.why: Jasur boshqa ishlarini chetga surib qoʻysa ulgurishini, lekin oylik hisobotini kimdir oʻz zimmasiga olishi kerakligini aytadi.

q.q: Who is going to put the slides together?
q.why: Rachel "I'll put the slides together myself that evening" deydi; Emily esa faqat oylik hisobotni oladi.

o: He isn't happy about it, but he's willing to make it work
He's excited because he enjoys working under pressure
He doesn't care because it isn't really his project
He's so upset that he refuses to change his plans
q.q: How does Jasur probably feel about the new date?
q.why: U avval eʼtiroz bildiradi va oxirida hazil bilan noroziligini sezdiradi, lekin shartini aytib rozi boʻladi: "All right, deal".

listening.title: A Change of Plans

o: Her salary was too low to pay her rent
She had almost no money left at the end of each month
She made mistakes with her company's money
She owed money to her sister
q.q: What was Madina's problem before last year?
q.why: Matnda "At the end of every month she had almost nothing left" deyilgan - oy oxirida puli deyarli qolmas edi.

o: She cooked every meal at home
She wrote down everything she spent
She paid for everything in cash
q.q: What did Madina do for thirty days?
q.why: U oʻttiz kun davomida har bir xarajatini, hatto bir piyola kofe va avtobus chiptasini ham daftarga yozib bordi.

o: How much she was spending on eating out and delivery
How much she had already saved
q.why: Maoshining deyarli beshdan biri tashqarida ovqatlanish va taom yetkazib berishga ketayotgani uni hayratga soldi.

o: Because she pays for her subscriptions that day
So the money is saved before she can spend it
q.q: Why does the transfer to her savings account happen on payday?
q.why: Matnda "before she can spend it" deyilgan: pul sarflanib ketmasidan oldin jamgʻarma hisobiga oʻtadi.

o: People should stop going to restaurants
Tracking your spending helps you see and change your habits
Only people with high salaries can save money
Accountants are always careful with their own money
q.q: What is the main idea of the text?
q.why: Oxirgi gaplar asosiy fikrni beradi: daftar uni boyitmadi, balki pul qayerga ketayotganini koʻrsatdi va shu orqali odatlarini oʻzgartirishga yordam berdi.

reading.text:
Madina is 29 and works as an accountant in Tashkent. She is good with her company's money, but until last year she was not very careful with her own. At the end of every month she had almost nothing left, and she could not understand why.

In January she decided to try something simple. For thirty days she wrote down everything she spent in a small notebook, even a cup of coffee or a bus ticket. The results surprised her. She was spending almost a fifth of her salary on eating out and food delivery. She also found three subscriptions that she had forgotten about and never used.

Madina did not stop going to restaurants completely, because she enjoys meeting her friends there. Instead, she started cooking at home on weekdays and canceled the subscriptions. She also set up an automatic transfer, so ten percent of her salary goes into a savings account on payday, before she can spend it.

A year later, Madina has saved enough for a trip to Istanbul with her sister. She says the notebook did not make her richer. It just showed her where the money was going.
reading.title: Madina's Money Notebook

o: They allow businesses to raise prices
They remove the cost of handling cash
q.q: According to the first paragraph, how do digital payments help businesses?
q.why: Birinchi xatboshida raqamli toʻlovlar bizneslarni naqd pulni sanash, saqlash va tashish xarajatidan xalos qilishi aytilgan.

o: Recorded transactions are easier to tax
Printing bills and coins is expensive
Banks pay governments for payment data
Most citizens have asked for them
q.q: Why do governments find digital payments attractive?
q.why: Ikkinchi xatboshiga koʻra, bank orqali oʻtgan toʻlovlardan soliq olish hech qayerda qayd etilmagan naqd puldan ancha oson.

q.q: In the third paragraph, the phrase "shut out" is closest in meaning to:
q.why: "Shut out" - chetda qoldirilmoq degani: doʻkon naqd pul olmay qoʻysa, naqd pulga tayanadigan odamlar xarid qila olmay qoladi.

o: People who pay with cash usually earn less
Paying digitally can make it harder to control spending
Most shoppers still prefer cash to cards
Stores earn less from card payments than from cash
q.q: What can be inferred from the studies mentioned in the third paragraph?
q.why: Odamlar karta yoki telefon bilan toʻlaganda erkinroq sarflaydi, demak, xarajatni nazorat qilish qiyinlashadi - bu matnda ochiq aytilmagan, lekin undan kelib chiqadigan xulosa.

o: Cash will soon become popular again
Digital payments are too risky to rely on
Governments should stop encouraging digital payments
Cash will keep declining, so people who depend on it need protection
q.q: Which statement best matches the writer's view?
q.why: Oxirgi xatboshida muallif naqd pul kamayishda davom etishini aytadi va asosiy masala - raqamli pul hali qulay boʻlmagan odamlarni himoya qilish ekanini taʼkidlaydi.

reading.text:
Ten years ago, paying for a cup of coffee with a phone seemed like a novelty. Today, in many cities, it is cash that looks unusual. Digital payments have spread faster than most economists predicted, and the reasons are not hard to find. They are quick, they leave a record, and they spare businesses the cost of counting, storing and transporting bills and coins.

For governments, the shift has an additional appeal. Transactions that pass through banks are far easier to tax than cash that changes hands unrecorded. This is one reason why many governments actively encourage card and mobile payments.

However, the benefits are not evenly distributed. Older people, rural residents and those without a bank account often depend on cash, and they can find themselves shut out when stores stop accepting it. There is also a psychological cost. A number of studies suggest that people spend more freely when they tap a card or a phone than when they hand over physical money, apparently because the payment feels less real. For households that are already struggling to save, this is not a trivial concern.

Privacy is a further issue. Every digital payment creates data about where a person was and what they bought, and it is not always clear who has access to that information or how long it is kept.

None of this means that the trend will reverse. Most researchers expect cash to keep declining. The more realistic question is whether societies can enjoy the convenience of digital money while protecting the people for whom it is not yet a convenient option at all.
reading.title: The Quiet Decline of Cash

speaking.q: Tell me about yourself. Where do you live, and what do you do?
speaking.uz: Oʻzingiz haqingizda gapirib bering. Qayerda yashaysiz va nima ish qilasiz?

speaking.q: Do you think it's better to work from home or at the office? Why?
speaking.uz: Sizningcha, uydan ishlagan yaxshimi yoki ofisdami? Nima uchun?

speaking.q: How is the way people pay for things today different from ten years ago? Explain why you think it has changed.
speaking.uz: Odamlarning bugungi toʻlov qilish usuli oʻn yil oldingidan nimasi bilan farq qiladi? Nima uchun oʻzgargan deb oʻylaysiz, tushuntiring.

vocab.q: I ___ a shower every morning before work.
vocab.why: Amerika ingliz tilida "take a shower" deyiladi; "dush qabul qilmoq" ni soʻzma-soʻz "accept" yoki "make" bilan tarjima qilib boʻlmaydi.

vocab.q: Excuse me, how much does this jacket ___?
vocab.why: Narsaning narxi haqida "cost" feʼli ishlatiladi; "pay" va "spend" ni odam bajaradi, "price" esa ot.

vocab.q: I was late for work because I ___ the bus.
vocab.why: Transportga ulgurmay qolish "miss the bus" deyiladi; "lose" esa narsani yoʻqotib qoʻyishni bildiradi.

vocab.q: My pen isn't working. Can I ___ yours for a second?
vocab.why: "Borrow" - birovdan vaqtincha olmoq, "lend" esa birovga vaqtincha bermoq; bu yerda gapiruvchi oladi.

vocab.q: It's really cold outside. Don't forget to ___ your coat.
vocab.why: Kiyimni kiyish harakati "put on" deyiladi; "dress" dan keyin kiyim nomi toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri kelmaydi, "take off" esa yechmoq degani.

vocab.q: I'm looking for a new ___ because my salary is too low.
vocab.why: "Job" sanaladigan ot (a job - ish oʻrni), "work" esa sanalmaydi va "a" artikli bilan kelmaydi.

vocab.q: I'm really ___ forward to seeing you next week.
vocab.why: "Look forward to" - biror narsani intiqlik bilan kutmoq degan turgʻun birikma; "wait" bilan bunday aytilmaydi.

vocab.q: Could you ___ me a favor and print this for me?
vocab.why: "Do someone a favor" - birovning iltimosini bajarmoq degan turgʻun birikma; "favor" soʻzi "make" bilan ishlatilmaydi.

vocab.q: I can't ___ to buy a new car right now. They're too expensive.
vocab.why: "can't afford to" - biror narsaga puli (qurbi) yetmaslik; "allow" esa ruxsat bermoq degani.

vocab.q: We ran ___ printer paper, so I ordered some more.
vocab.why: "Run out of" - biror narsa tugab qolmoq degan frazali feʼl: We ran out of paper.

vocab.q: The ___ for the report is Friday, so we need to hurry.
vocab.why: Ishni topshirishning oxirgi muddati "deadline" deyiladi; "term" va "period" vaqt oraligʻini bildiradi.

vocab.q: Please ___ out this form and sign it at the bottom.
vocab.why: Anketa yoki blankani toʻldirish Amerika ingliz tilida "fill out a form" deyiladi.

vocab.q: Our flight was delayed, so we ___ up missing our connection.
vocab.why: "End up" + -ing - oxir-oqibat (kutilmagan holda) biror ahvolga tushib qolmoq degan frazali feʼl.

vocab.q: We need to ___ up with a better idea before the meeting.
vocab.why: "Come up with" - yangi gʻoya yoki yechim oʻylab topmoq degan frazali feʼl.

vocab.q: We need to cut ___ on travel expenses this quarter.
vocab.why: "Cut back on" - xarajat yoki isteʼmolni kamaytirmoq; "cut off" - uzib qoʻymoq, "cut out" - butunlay chiqarib tashlamoq.

vocab.q: I have a really ___ schedule this week, so I can't take on anything new.
vocab.why: Boʻsh vaqt deyarli qolmagan jadval "a tight schedule" deyiladi; "zich jadval" ni "dense" deb soʻzma-soʻz tarjima qilib boʻlmaydi.

vocab.q: We worked all weekend to ___ the deadline.
vocab.why: Ishni belgilangan muddatga ulgurtirish "meet a deadline" deyiladi - bu turgʻun birikma, boshqa feʼllar "deadline" bilan bunday maʼno bermaydi.

vocab.q: I can't ___ up with this noise anymore. I'm going to talk to the neighbors.
vocab.why: "Put up with" - yoqmagan narsaga chidamoq, toqat qilmoq degan frazali feʼl.

writing.prompt: Write about 100-120 words. Describe your job (what you do and what a typical workday looks like) and explain why you are learning English.
writing.uz: Taxminan 100-120 soʻz yozing. Ishingizni tasvirlang (nima ish qilasiz, odatdagi ish kuningiz qanday oʻtadi) va nima uchun ingliz tilini oʻrganayotganingizni tushuntiring. Lugʻat yoki tarjimondan foydalanmang - bu matn hozirgi darajangizni aniqlash uchun kerak.
